Of course. What's the problem?
I don't understand this question.
Let's read it together. What does it ask?
How many apples are left after we eat 5.
How many apples are there at the start?
12. So 12 minus 5 is 7!
Exactly! Well done.
Thanks, Maya! That was easy.

conversations.title: Discussing exam dates and preparation.
conversations.scene: The final exam is coming, and Yuki wants to be ready.

lines.text: When is the final exam?
On the 20th of June, at 9 in the morning.
What's in the exam?
Reading, listening, writing and a short conversation.
How can I prepare?
Do the practice tests in the book, and read a little every day.
Can we bring a dictionary?
No, I'm sorry. No dictionaries and no phones.
OK. I'll start studying this weekend.

conversations.title: Borrowing a book from the library.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to borrow a photography book.

lines.text: Hello. I'd like to borrow this book.
Do you have a library card?
No. Can I get one?
Yes, it's free. I need your ID and your address.
Here you are.
Here's your card. You can keep the book for three weeks.
Can I renew it online?
Yes, on our website. Once or twice.
Perfect. Thank you!

conversations.title: Attending a parent-teacher meeting.
conversations.scene: Leon meets Timo's teacher at the school.

lines.text: Thank you for coming. Timo is doing well at school.
That's good to hear. How is he with the other children?
He has lots of friends. He's very kind.
And are there any problems?
Sometimes he talks too much in class. He finds it hard to sit still.
Yes, that sounds like Timo!
His reading is very good, but he needs more practice with math.
What can we do at home?
Ten minutes of math games every day would help.
OK, we'll do that. Thank you very much.

conversations.title: Finding a language exchange partner and arranging practice.
conversations.scene: Maya meets someone from a language exchange website.

lines.text: Hi! Are you Maya, from the language exchange?
Yes! Nice to meet you. Thanks for coming.
So, you want to practice the language, and I want to practice English.
Exactly. How shall we do it?
Half an hour in each language?
Perfect. Can you correct my mistakes?
Of course, if you correct mine.
Deal. How often can we meet?
Once a week? Thursdays after work are good for me.
Thursdays are great. Same place, same time?

conversations.title: Inviting someone for coffee.
conversations.scene: Leon finally asks Maya to have a coffee with him.

lines.text: Maya, are you free on Saturday morning?
I think so. Why?
Would you like to have a coffee with me?
Sure, I'd love to!
Great. Do you know the café by the park?
The one with the blue chairs?
Yes. Is 10 o'clock OK?
Perfect. See you there!

conversations.title: Accepting or politely declining an invitation.
conversations.scene: Nora invites Maya to two things this week.

lines.text: Maya, would you like to come to my birthday dinner on Friday?
I'd love to! Thank you for inviting me.
Great. And on Sunday, we're going hiking. Do you want to join?
That sounds fun, but I'm afraid I can't. My friend Omar arrives that day.
Oh, no problem. Maybe next time.
Definitely. What can I bring on Friday?
Nothing, just yourself!
OK. See you on Friday.

conversations.title: Organizing a dinner or birthday party with friends.
conversations.scene: Leon, Yuki and Omar plan a surprise party for Maya.

lines.text: So, Maya's birthday is next Saturday. Let's have a surprise party.
Great idea! Where?
Here, at my place. I'll cook.
I'll bring the drinks and the music.
I'll make the cake. And who will invite people?
Omar, can you send a message to everyone? But not to Maya!
Of course. What time should people come?
At 7. Maya comes home at 8.
Perfect. And don't tell her, Omar!
Me? I never say anything!

conversations.title: Talking about your hobbies and interests.
conversations.scene: Maya and Leon have their coffee and talk about free time.

lines.text: So, what do you do in your free time?
I love painting. And I go running on weekends.
Painting! What do you paint?
Mostly landscapes. And you? What are your hobbies?
Cooking, of course. And I play the guitar.
Really? Do you play in a band?
No, just at home. Timo sings with me.
That's lovely. I'd like to hear you play.

conversations.title: Getting to know someone on a first date.
conversations.scene: Leon and Maya go on their first real date.

lines.text: I'm really glad you said yes to dinner.
Me too. This place is lovely.
So tell me, what do you miss most about home?
My family, and the snow. And you? Have you always lived here?
Yes, all my life. But I traveled a lot when I was younger.
Where was your favorite place?
Japan. Maybe Yuki can teach me some words.
I'm sure she'd love that. Do you think you'll travel again one day?
I hope so. Maybe with good company.

conversations.title: Meeting your partner's family.
conversations.scene: Leon takes Maya to Sunday lunch with his parents.

lines.text: Mom, Dad, this is Maya.
Hello! It's so nice to meet you. Thank you for inviting me.
Welcome, Maya! Leon talks about you all the time.
Mom!
Come in, come in. Do you like roast chicken?
I love it. These flowers are for you.
Oh, how beautiful! Thank you. Please, sit down.
So, Maya, Leon says you're a designer?
Yes, I work for a design company in the city.
And how do you like living here?
I love it. Everybody is so friendly.

conversations.title: Making plans for the weekend.
conversations.scene: Omar has just arrived, and they plan the weekend.

lines.text: So, what do you want to do this weekend?
I don't know. What do you suggest?
On Saturday, the market and the old town?
Great. And on Sunday?
Let's go to the lake. Leon has a car.
Perfect. What time shall we meet?
At 9 at my place. Don't be late!
Me? Never.

conversations.title: Discussing different opinions without causing an argument.
conversations.scene: Nora and Maya disagree about a new building in the city.

lines.text: Have you seen the new tower by the river? I think it's ugly.
Really? I actually like it. It's modern and bright.
But it doesn't fit with the old buildings.
I see your point. But cities need new things too.
Maybe. But why there, next to the old bridge?
That's true, the place isn't perfect.
Well, we can agree to disagree.
Exactly. And we both agree the coffee here is great.
That's true.

conversations.title: Apologizing to a friend after a misunderstanding.
conversations.scene: Maya forgot Yuki's photo exhibition, and Yuki is hurt.

lines.text: Yuki, I'm really sorry about last night.
I waited for you. I was a bit sad.
I know. I mixed up the dates. It was a stupid mistake.
I feel terrible. Can I make it up to you?
It's OK. I know you're busy.
That's no excuse. Is the exhibition still open?
Yes, until Sunday.
Then let's go together on Saturday. And lunch is on me.
OK, deal. Thanks for saying sorry.

conversations.title: Staying in touch and arranging to meet again.
conversations.scene: Omar's visit is over, and Maya takes him to the station.

lines.text: I can't believe I'm leaving already.
Me neither. It went so fast.
Let's stay in touch. Send me photos of everything.
I will. And call me when you get home.
When can we meet again?
Maybe at Christmas, when I visit home?
Perfect. I'll count the days.
Do you have your passport, your phone and your wallet?
Yes, yes and yes! See? I'm learning.
Have a safe trip, Omar.

conversations.title: Buying tickets and entering a museum.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to visit the art museum.

lines.text: Hello. One ticket, please.
Are you a student?
Yes, here's my student card.
Then it's 8 euros instead of 14.
Can I take photos inside?
Yes, but without flash.
Where can I leave my bag?
In the lockers, on the left.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Joining a guided city tour and asking questions.
conversations.scene: Omar joins a walking tour of the old town.

lines.text: Welcome, everyone! This tour takes two hours.
Excuse me, how old is this church?
About 700 years old. It's the oldest building in the city.
Can we go inside?
Yes, at the end of the tour.
And who is the statue in the square?
A famous poet. He wrote about this city.
Will we stop for a break?
Yes, after an hour, at a nice café.
Great, thanks!

conversations.title: Buying cinema tickets and choosing seats.
conversations.scene: Maya and Leon want to see a movie on Friday night.

lines.text: Two tickets for the 8 o'clock movie, please.
Where would you like to sit?
In the middle, not too close to the screen.
Row 9, seats 12 and 13?
Perfect.
Is the movie in the original language?
Yes, with subtitles. That's 22 euros.
Here you are. Where can I buy popcorn?
Right over there.

conversations.title: Attending a concert or live performance.
conversations.scene: Maya and Yuki go to a jazz concert.

lines.text: Tickets, please.
Here, on my phone.
Thank you. The concert starts at 8. You can't go in during the songs.
Where are our seats?
Balcony, row 2. Take the stairs on the right.
Is there a break?
Yes, 20 minutes, after an hour.
Can we get a drink in the break?
Yes, the bar is on the first floor.
Great. I'm so excited!

conversations.title: Joining a gym and asking about membership.
conversations.scene: Nora wants to start training at the gym near the office.

lines.text: Hi. How much is a membership?
35 euros a month, or 300 for a year.
Do I have to sign a contract?
For the monthly one, it's three months minimum.
Are the classes included?
Yes, yoga, spinning and boxing, all included.
What are the opening hours?
Every day from 6 in the morning to 11 at night.
Can I try it first?
Of course. Your first day is free.

conversations.title: Participating in a sports activity with local people.
conversations.scene: Leon takes Omar to his Sunday soccer game in the park.

lines.text: Hi, Leon! Who's your friend?
This is Omar. He's visiting. Can he play with us?
Of course! Omar, do you play often?
Not really, but I love it. Where do you need me?
Can you play in defense?
Sure. Which team am I on?
The blue team. Here's a shirt.
Thanks. How long do we play?
An hour, and then we all go for a drink together.
Even better!

conversations.title: Asking about hiking trails and outdoor safety.
conversations.scene: Maya and Omar plan a hike and ask about safety.

lines.text: Hello. Can you recommend a hiking trail for this weekend?
How much experience do you have?
Some. We can walk for four or five hours.
Then try the lake trail. It's beautiful, and not too difficult.
Is it safe? Are there any dangerous parts?
There's one steep part, so wear good shoes.
What about the weather?
Check the forecast before you go. Storms come fast in the mountains.
Is there phone signal on the trail?
Not everywhere. Tell someone your plans, and take a map.

conversations.title: Renting equipment at a beach or ski resort.
conversations.scene: Omar rents skis for his first day on the snow.

lines.text: Hi. I'd like to rent skis for one day.
Sure. Are you a beginner?
Yes, it's my first time.
What's your shoe size, and how tall are you?
Size 44, and I'm 1.80 meters.
Then these skis and these boots. Try the boots on.
They're a bit tight.
Let's try a size bigger.
Much better. How much is it for the day?
35 euros, with a helmet. Bring them back by 5.

conversations.title: Visiting a historical monument and asking about its history.
conversations.scene: Yuki visits the old fortress above the city.

lines.text: Excuse me, when was this fortress built?
In the 13th century, to protect the city.
Who lived here?
Soldiers, and later the city's prisoners.
Wow. Is it true there's a secret tunnel?
Yes! It goes down to the river. You can see the entrance.
Can I take photos of it?
Of course. The best view is from the tower.
Thank you, that's so interesting.

conversations.title: Requesting a refund after an event is canceled.
conversations.scene: The open-air concert was canceled because of the rain.

lines.text: Hello. The concert last night was canceled. Can I get a refund?
Yes, of course. Do you have your tickets?
Here, two tickets. They were 45 euros each.
You can get your money back, or new tickets for the new date.
When is the new date?
The 12th of next month.
I'm traveling then. I'd like the refund, please.
No problem. The money will be back on your card in five days.
Do I need to fill in anything?
No, I just need your email address.

conversations.title: Setting up your phone's mobile internet connection.
conversations.scene: Omar's new SIM card works for calls, but not for the internet.

lines.text: Hi. I bought this SIM card yesterday, but the internet doesn't work.
Let me see. Is mobile data turned on?
I think so.
Yes, but the settings are wrong. Can I have your phone?
Sure.
I'm changing the network settings. Now, restart the phone.
OK. Oh! It works now.
Will I need to do this again?
No, only once. You're ready.
Great. Thanks so much.

conversations.title: Calling technical support about a broken internet connection.
conversations.scene: Maya's internet has been down all morning, and she works from home today.

lines.text: Technical support, how can I help you?
Hello. My internet hasn't worked since this morning.
Can you give me your customer number?
Thank you. Are the lights on your router green or red?
The internet light is red. The others are green.
Please turn the router off, wait 30 seconds, and turn it on again.
OK, I did it. It's still red.
Then the problem is on our side. A technician can come tomorrow.
Tomorrow? I'm working from home today. Is there anything faster?
I'm sorry. I'll give you 20 gigabytes of free mobile data today.

conversations.title: Asking someone to help you print or scan a document.
conversations.scene: Maya needs to scan a document, but the new printer is complicated.

lines.text: Sorry, can you help me with the printer?
Sure. What do you need?
I need to scan this contract and send it by email.
Put it face down here. Then choose "Scan to email".
Where do I type the email address?
On this screen. Use the keyboard here.
And can I print a copy too?
Yes, press the copy button. One copy?
Two, please. Thank you, you're a lifesaver.

conversations.title: Explaining a problem with an app or website.
conversations.scene: The banking app on Yuki's phone keeps closing.

lines.text: Hello, how can I help you?
Hi. Your app keeps closing when I try to log in.
Which phone do you have?
It's an Android phone, about two years old.
Have you updated the app?
Yes, yesterday. The problem started after the update.
Some users have the same problem. We're working on it.
Is there another way to make a payment today?
Yes, you can use our website in your phone's browser.
OK. When will the app work again?
We hope by the end of the week.

conversations.title: Recovering access to an online account.
conversations.scene: Omar can't log in to his email account on his new phone.

lines.text: Hi. I can't log in to my account. I forgot my password.
No problem. Did you click on "Forgot password"?
Yes, but the code goes to my old phone number. That phone was stolen.
I see. Do you have a backup email address?
I'm not sure.
Then I need to check your identity. What's your date of birth?
The 4th of May, 1995.
And can you name two recent emails in your inbox?
One from Maya, and one from my airline.
Thank you. I'm sending a link to set a new password.

conversations.title: Contacting customer support about an online order.
conversations.scene: Nora ordered a lamp online, but she received the wrong one.

lines.text: Customer service, how can I help?
Hello. I ordered a white lamp, but you sent a black one.
I'm sorry. Can I have your order number?
Thank you. Yes, I see the mistake.
Can you send me the white one?
Of course. And we'll send you a free return label.
Do I need to pay for the return?
No, it's free. Just put the black lamp in the box.
Great. Thank you for your help.

conversations.title: Correcting a wrong delivery address.
conversations.scene: Maya realizes she sent a gift to her old address.

lines.text: Hello. I made an order this morning, but the address is wrong.
No problem. Has it been sent yet?
I don't know. The order number is 22 41 905.
Let me check. No, it's still in our warehouse.
Great. Can you change the address, please?
Of course. What's the new address?
Linden Street 22, apartment 3.
Done. The package will arrive on Thursday.
Thank you! That's a relief.

conversations.title: Asking about a delayed or missing package.
conversations.scene: Leon's package was supposed to arrive a week ago.

lines.text: Hello. My package should have arrived last week, but it's not here.
I'm sorry. Do you have the tracking number?
Thank you. The tracking says it was delivered on Tuesday.
Delivered? But I didn't get anything.
Did you check with your neighbors, or at the front door?
Yes, I asked everyone. Nobody has it.
Then I'll open an investigation. If we can't find it, we'll send a new one.
How long will that take?
Five working days at the most.

conversations.title: Canceling an online subscription.
conversations.scene: Nora wants to cancel a streaming service she never uses.

lines.text: Hello, how can I help you today?
Hi. I'd like to cancel my subscription.
I'm sorry to hear that. May I ask why?
I don't have time to watch anything.
We can offer you three months for half the price.
No, thank you. I'd just like to cancel it.
OK. Your subscription ends on the 30th.
Will I be charged again?
No, this was your last payment. You'll get an email to confirm.
Thank you.

conversations.title: Solving a problem with an online payment.
conversations.scene: Yuki paid for a course online, and the money left her account twice.

lines.text: Hello. I paid for a course on your website, but I was charged twice.
I'm sorry about that. Can you give me the date and the amount?
Yesterday, 120 euros. I see two payments in my bank account.
Let me look. Yes, there are two payments. The second one is a mistake.
Can you give me the money back?
Yes. I've started the refund now.
When will I see it in my account?
In three to five working days.
Can you send me a confirmation by email?
Of course. It will arrive in a few minutes.

conversations.title: Attending a wedding and congratulating the couple.
conversations.scene: Nora is getting married, and Maya and Leon are at the party.

lines.text: Congratulations, Nora! You look beautiful.
Thank you, Maya! I'm so happy you're here.
Congratulations! It was a lovely ceremony.
Thank you, Leon. Did you like the music?
Very much. The band is great.
We wish you all the happiness in the world.
That's so sweet. Now come, let's dance!
Just one thing: where do we leave the gift?
On the table by the door. Thank you so much!

conversations.title: Attending a funeral and expressing condolences.
conversations.scene: Greta's old friend has died, and Maya goes to the funeral.

lines.text: Greta, I'm so sorry for your loss.
Thank you for coming, Maya. It means a lot.
How long did you know her?
Fifty years. We were teachers at the same school.
She must have been a wonderful friend.
She was. She always made me laugh.
If you need anything, I'm right upstairs.
You're very kind. Will you come for tea tomorrow?
Of course.

conversations.title: Visiting a place of worship and asking about local customs.
conversations.scene: Yuki visits the old cathedral and wants to be respectful.

lines.text: Excuse me, can tourists come in?
Yes, but not during the service on Sunday mornings.
Is there a dress code?
Please cover your shoulders. You can borrow a scarf here.
Can I take photos inside?
Yes, but please be quiet, and no flash.
Should I take off my hat?
Yes, men and women usually take off their hats.
Thank you for explaining.

conversations.title: Participating in a local festival or traditional celebration.
conversations.scene: Leon takes Omar and Timo to the city's summer festival.

lines.text: Wow, so many people! What's the festival for?
It's the city's birthday. It's 800 years old this year.
Dad, can we see the dancers?
Yes, they start at 6, in the main square.
What are those people wearing?
Traditional costumes. Everybody wears them today.
And what's that smell? It's delicious.
Grilled sausages and sweet bread. Let's try some.
And then the fireworks!
Yes, at 10. You can stay up late tonight.

conversations.title: Explaining your dietary restrictions at someone's home.
conversations.scene: Leon invites Yuki to dinner, and she tells him what she can't eat.

lines.text: Yuki, I'm making dinner on Saturday. Is there anything you don't eat?
Thank you for asking. I'm allergic to nuts, and I don't eat meat.
No meat and no nuts. Do you eat fish?
Yes, fish and eggs are fine.
How about baked fish with vegetables?
That sounds perfect.
And for dessert, a lemon cake. No nuts, I promise.
Thank you, Leon. I hope it's not too much trouble.
Not at all. I love cooking for friends.

conversations.title: Asking for help with childcare or enrolling a child in daycare.
conversations.scene: Leon asks about after-school care for Timo.

lines.text: Hello. I'm looking for after-school care for my son.
How old is he?
He's seven. School finishes at 1, but I work until 5.
We take children from 1 to 6, Monday to Friday.
Is there lunch?
Yes, a warm lunch, and help with homework.
How much does it cost?
220 euros a month, with lunch.
Do you have a free place?
Yes, from September. Please fill in this form.
Great. Can Timo come and see it first?
Of course. Come on Friday afternoon.

conversations.title: Taking a pet to the veterinarian.
conversations.scene: Greta's old dog hasn't eaten for two days.

lines.text: Hello. What's wrong with him today?
He hasn't eaten for two days, and he sleeps all the time.
How old is he?
Twelve.
Is he drinking water?
A little, yes.
Let me examine him. His stomach is a bit sensitive.
Is it serious?
I don't think so. Give him this medicine and some rice with chicken.
Thank you. He's my best friend, you know.
I understand. Call me if he doesn't eat tomorrow.

conversations.title: Crossing an international border by car and answering questions.
conversations.scene: Leon and Maya drive to the neighboring country for a weekend.

lines.text: Good morning. Passports, please.
Here you are. Both of them.
Where are you going?
To the lakes, for the weekend.
Whose car is this?
It's my car. Here are the papers.
Do you have anything to declare? Alcohol or cigarettes?
No, just our bags and some food.
Please open the trunk.
Of course.
Thank you. Have a nice trip.

conversations.title: Explaining a cultural misunderstanding and asking about local etiquette.
conversations.scene: At dinner, Yuki thinks she has done something wrong.

lines.text: Leon, can I ask you something? I think I made a mistake.
Sure. What happened?
When I met your mother, she kissed me on both cheeks. I didn't move.
Don't worry, she wasn't offended.
In Japan, we bow. Is the kiss normal here?
With family and friends, yes. With strangers, just a handshake.
And what about at work?
At work, always a handshake. And people use first names.
That's very different from home. Thank you for explaining.
Any time. And next time, just kiss her back!

conversations.title: Handling an unexpected situation when nobody speaks your language.
conversations.scene: In a small village, Omar needs a charger, and the shop owner speaks no English.

lines.text: Hello. Do you speak English?
No, sorry. Only a little.
OK, no problem. I need this. For my phone.
Ah, a charger! For this phone?
Yes! The battery is almost dead.
I have this one. Try it.
Can you write the price, please?
Here. 12 euros.
Perfect. Thank you so much!
You're welcome. Your language is good!

conversations.title: Asking a local what you absolutely shouldn't miss in the city.
conversations.scene: Omar is back in the city for the summer, and he asks Leon what he shouldn't miss.

lines.text: Leon, what should I absolutely not miss in the city?
The old town, of course. And the view from the castle.
I saw those last time. Something new?
Then the Sunday flea market by the river. You'll love it.
Great. And for food?
The fish soup at the harbor. It's the best in the country.
Anything else?
Take the old tram, line 1, all the way to the end. It's beautiful.
Perfect. I'll do it all this week.

conversations.title: Finding the most beautiful streets and neighborhoods to explore.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to take photos of the city's most beautiful streets.

lines.text: Which streets are the most beautiful for walking?
Try Rose Lane in the old town. It's full of flowers.
Is it far from here?
Ten minutes. And the artists' quarter is right behind it.
What's special about the artists' quarter?
Colorful houses, small galleries and lots of street art.
When is the best light for photos?
Early in the morning, before the tourists come.
Thank you! I'll get up early tomorrow.

conversations.title: Asking where the historic old town begins.
conversations.scene: Maya and Omar want to start their walk in the historic old town.

lines.text: Excuse me, where does the old town begin?
At the big stone gate, at the end of this street.
Is it far?
No, two minutes. You'll see the clock tower.
Can cars drive in the old town?
No, it's only for people on foot.
Great. Is there a map at the gate?
Yes, there's a big map and a tourist office.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Finding the best viewpoint overlooking the city.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants a photo of the whole city from above.

lines.text: Where is the best viewpoint over the city?
The castle hill, or the tower of the cathedral.
Which one is better at sunset?
The castle hill. You can see the river and the mountains.
How do I get up there?
Walk up the steps, or take the little train from Market Street.
Does it cost anything?
The steps are free. The little train is 3 euros.
I'll walk up and take the train down!

conversations.title: Asking which attractions are within walking distance.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to see the sights without a bus or a taxi.

lines.text: Which sights are within walking distance?
The cathedral, the old town and the market are all close.
How far is the cathedral?
About ten minutes on foot.
And the museum?
Twenty minutes. Or take bus 4.
I'll walk. Do you have a map?
Yes, here you are. I'll mark the best route.

conversations.title: Discovering interesting places that aren't in tourist guides.
conversations.scene: Maya asks Leon about places that tourists don't know.

lines.text: Leon, do you know any places that aren't in the guidebooks?
Of course! There's a secret garden behind the old library.
A secret garden? How do I get in?
Through the small door in the courtyard. It's open in the afternoon.
What else?
A tiny bakery under the bridge. It opens at 6 in the morning.
Is it worth getting up so early?
Absolutely. Their cinnamon rolls are amazing.
OK, I'll try. Don't tell the tourists!

conversations.title: Asking where locals usually spend their free time.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to spend a free afternoon like a local.

lines.text: Where do people here usually go in their free time?
In summer, everybody goes to the river beach.
A beach by the river?
Yes, with sand, cafés and music. It's very popular.
And in the evening?
People meet in the small squares for a drink.
Which square do you like best?
Fountain Square. It's lively, but not too touristy.
Thanks for the tip!

conversations.title: Finding a pleasant place to walk in the evening.
conversations.scene: After dinner, Maya wants a quiet walk.

lines.text: Is there a nice place for a walk in the evening?
Yes, the path along the river.
Is it safe at night?
Yes, it's well lit, and there are always people.
How long is it?
About an hour to the old bridge and back.
Are there any cafés on the way?
Yes, a few. The ice cream at the bridge is very good.
Perfect, thank you.

conversations.title: Asking whether a particular attraction is worth visiting.
conversations.scene: Omar isn't sure if the famous tower is worth the money.

lines.text: Is the TV tower worth visiting?
The view is great, but the tickets are expensive.
How much are they?
22 euros. And there's often a long line.
Is there anything similar, but cheaper?
The cathedral tower. It's only 5 euros, and the view is almost the same.
Is it good for photos?
Definitely. And it's in the middle of the old town.
Then the cathedral tower it is. Thanks!

conversations.title: Planning a sightseeing route for just one day.
conversations.scene: Maya helps Omar plan a sightseeing route for his last free day.

lines.text: I only have one free day left. What should I see?
Let's plan a route. Start with the market in the morning.
OK. Then?
Walk through the old town to the cathedral. It opens at 10.
When should we have lunch?
At the harbor, around 1. The fish soup, remember?
Of course. And in the afternoon?
The museum, and then the castle hill for the sunset.
That's a lot. Will we have time?
Yes, if we don't stop at every café.
That will be the difficult part!

conversations.title: Asking where to buy tickets for a famous attraction.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to visit the castle, the city's most famous sight.

lines.text: Where can I buy tickets for the castle?
At the ticket office, on the left of the gate.
Can I buy them online too?
Yes, and online tickets are 2 euros cheaper.
Is there a line at the ticket office?
Today, about twenty minutes.
Then I'll buy one online now.
Good idea. Show the code on your phone here at the gate.

conversations.title: Finding out whether tickets need to be booked in advance.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to see the royal palace on Saturday.

lines.text: Royal Palace, good morning.
Hello. Do I need to book tickets in advance?
For the weekend, yes. It's often sold out.
Are there tickets for this Saturday?
Yes, at 11 or at 3.
Can I book one for 11?
Of course. You can pay online with this link.
Do I need to print the ticket?
No, the ticket on your phone is fine.

conversations.title: Asking whether you can enter without a guided tour.
conversations.scene: Yuki doesn't want to join a group tour.

lines.text: Can I visit without a guided tour?
Yes, but only the gardens and the first floor.
What about the royal rooms?
Those are only with a guide.
Is there an audio guide?
Yes, in eleven languages. It's 4 euros.
Great. Do you have one in Japanese?
Yes, we do. Here you are.

conversations.title: Understanding the opening and closing times of an attraction.
conversations.scene: Omar arrives at the museum on a Monday.

lines.text: Excuse me, what are the opening hours?
From 10 to 6, Tuesday to Sunday.
So it's closed today?
Yes, sorry. We're closed on Mondays.
What time do you close on Sunday?
At 5. The last entry is at 4.
OK. I'll come back tomorrow.
Come early. It's busy in the afternoon.

conversations.title: Asking how long it takes to explore a monument.
conversations.scene: Maya and Omar have two hours before their train.

lines.text: How long does it take to see the cathedral?
About an hour, with the tower.
And without the tower?
Thirty minutes. But the tower is the best part!
How many steps are there?
248. It takes about ten minutes to climb.
We have two hours. Let's do both.
OK, but slowly, please!

conversations.title: Finding out what is included in an entrance ticket.
conversations.scene: Yuki compares two tickets for the old fortress.

lines.text: What is included in the ticket?
The normal ticket is the fortress and the museum.
And the combined ticket?
It also includes the tower and a boat ride on the river.
How much is the combined ticket?
24 euros, and the normal one is 15.
Is the audio guide included?
Only with the combined ticket.
Then I'll take the combined one.

conversations.title: Asking whether photography and video recording are allowed.
conversations.scene: Yuki has her camera with her in the museum.

lines.text: Excuse me, can I take photos here?
Yes, but no flash, please.
What about videos?
Short videos are OK, but no tripods.
And in this room?
No photos in this room. The paintings are very old.
OK. Thank you for telling me.
You're welcome. Enjoy the museum.

conversations.title: Asking about the history of a famous building.
conversations.scene: Omar asks a guide about the old town hall.

lines.text: Excuse me, can you tell me about this building?
It's the old town hall. It was built in 1452.
Why is the tower crooked?
The ground is soft here, so the tower started to lean.
Is it dangerous?
No, it was repaired 50 years ago. It's safe.
What is it used for today?
Weddings, and a small museum about the city.
Can I go inside?
Yes, the museum is open every day except Monday.

conversations.title: Finding the entrance to a large tourist attraction.
conversations.scene: Maya walks around the palace, but every door is closed.

lines.text: Excuse me, where is the entrance?
Not here. This is the exit.
Oh! Where do I go?
Go around the building, to the right.
Is it far?
No, about five minutes. Look for the big flags.
Is the ticket office there too?
Yes, right next to the entrance.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking where to get the best photographs of a landmark.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants the perfect photo of the old bridge.

lines.text: Where's the best place to take photos of the bridge?
From the river path, on the other side.
Is it better in the morning or in the evening?
In the evening, when the lights come on.
Can I take photos from a boat?
Yes, the boat tours go under the bridge.
That sounds amazing.
Or go up the hill behind the church. You can see the whole river.
Thank you so much!

conversations.title: Asking locals which traditional dishes you should try.
conversations.scene: Omar asks Leon which local dishes he must try.

lines.text: Leon, which traditional dishes should I try?
Start with the fish soup. Every family has its own recipe.
What else?
Grilled meat with fresh bread and onions.
And something sweet?
The walnut cake! But don't give any to Yuki.
Right, her allergy. What's a typical breakfast?
Bread, cheese, tomatoes and strong coffee.
I'm hungry already.

conversations.title: Finding a restaurant where locals actually eat.
conversations.scene: Maya and Omar want to avoid the tourist restaurants.

lines.text: Excuse me, where do locals actually eat?
Not on the main square. That's for tourists.
Where then?
Try the small places behind the market.
Is there one you like?
My cousin's place, at the end of the street. Just the dish of the day.
Is it expensive?
No. Lunch is 12 euros, with soup and dessert.
That sounds perfect.

conversations.title: Asking what a regional specialty is made from.
conversations.scene: The waiter brings Maya the dish everybody talks about.

lines.text: This looks wonderful. What's it made from?
It's a regional specialty: lamb, potatoes and herbs.
How is it cooked?
Slowly, under a metal lid, with hot coals on top.
How long does it take?
About three hours. That's why you order it in advance.
What are the herbs?
Rosemary and bay leaves, from the hills.
It's delicious. Thank you for explaining.

conversations.title: Ordering a traditional breakfast in a local café.
conversations.scene: Yuki orders breakfast in a small café near her new apartment.

lines.text: Good morning! What can I get you?
Good morning. What is a traditional breakfast here?
Fresh bread, cheese, ham, tomatoes and coffee.
I don't eat meat. Can I have it without ham?
Of course. With an egg instead?
Yes, please. And a coffee with milk.
Anything else?
No, that's all. Thank you.

conversations.title: Asking a waiter to recommend the most popular dish.
conversations.scene: Omar can't decide what to order.

lines.text: What do you recommend?
Our most popular dish is the grilled fish.
What comes with it?
Potatoes and a salad.
Is the fish fresh?
Yes, from this morning.
Then I'll have the fish.
Great choice! And to drink?
A glass of white wine, please.

conversations.title: Trying street food and asking how it is prepared.
conversations.scene: Omar stops at a busy street food stand.

lines.text: That smells amazing! What is it?
Grilled corn and flatbread with cheese.
How do you make the flatbread?
Flour, water and salt. Then we cook it on this hot stone.
And what's inside?
Cheese and herbs. Or meat, if you like.
One with cheese, please. Is it spicy?
Only if you add this red sauce.
Just a little, please.

conversations.title: Visiting a bakery and choosing local pastries.
conversations.scene: Maya wants to try the local pastries.

lines.text: Good morning! What would you like?
What are these little cakes?
They're honey cakes. A local specialty.
And these, with the poppy seeds?
Poppy seed rolls. People eat them for breakfast.
I'll have two honey cakes and one roll, please.
Anything else?
No, thank you. How much is it?
4.20 euros.

conversations.title: Asking which dessert is typical of the region.
conversations.scene: After dinner, Nora wants to try a dessert from the region.

lines.text: Which dessert is typical of the region?
The plum dumplings. They're very popular.
What are they made of?
Potato dough with a whole plum inside, and sweet breadcrumbs.
Are they served warm?
Yes, warm, with a little cinnamon.
That sounds interesting. I'll try them.
You won't regret it.

conversations.title: Visiting a food market and sampling local products.
conversations.scene: Leon takes Omar to taste local products at the market.

lines.text: Would you like to try our cheese?
Yes, please! Is it made here?
Yes, from sheep's milk, in the mountains.
It's strong, but very good.
Try the dried ham too. It's famous here.
Here you are. It hangs for one year before we sell it.
Can I buy some to take home?
Of course. It's packed for travel, so it's fine on the plane.
Great. 200 grams of each, please.

conversations.title: Asking how a traditional dish is normally eaten.
conversations.scene: Yuki gets a dish she has never seen before.

lines.text: This looks great, but how do I eat it?
Tear a piece of bread and dip it in the sauce.
With my hands?
Yes, that's the traditional way.
And what about the meat?
Use the bread to pick up the meat too.
No fork at all?
You can have one, of course. But try it the local way!
OK, I'll try. It's delicious!

conversations.title: Asking how to reach the nearest beautiful beach.
conversations.scene: Maya and Yuki arrive in Belmar and want to go straight to the sea.

lines.text: Excuse me, how do we get to the nearest beach?
Go down this street to the end. Then turn left.
Is it a nice beach?
It's OK, but it's busy. North Beach is more beautiful.
How far is North Beach?
Twenty minutes on foot, or five by bus.
Which bus?
Number 2, from the stop over there.

conversations.title: Finding out which beaches are free and which require payment.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to know why some beaches cost money.

lines.text: Excuse me, is this beach free?
This part is private. It's 15 euros for a sunbed.
Are there any free beaches?
Yes, the public beach is after the pier.
What's the difference?
Here you get sunbeds, umbrellas and showers. There it's just sand.
Are there showers on the public beach?
Yes, but only cold ones.
That's fine. I'll go there.

conversations.title: Renting a sunbed and umbrella.
conversations.scene: Maya and Yuki want to spend the whole day on the beach.

lines.text: Hi. Can we rent two sunbeds and an umbrella?
For the whole day or half a day?
The whole day, please.
That's 25 euros.
Can we choose the place?
Yes, the front row is free.
Great. Can we pay by card?
Yes. Here's your ticket. Show it if someone asks.

conversations.title: Asking where it is safe to swim.
conversations.scene: There's a red flag on the beach, and Omar wants to swim.

lines.text: Excuse me, is it safe to swim today?
Not here. The red flag means strong currents.
Where can I swim then?
Between the yellow flags, near the pier. It's safer there.
How deep is it?
It gets deep quickly, after about twenty meters.
Are there jellyfish?
A few this week. If one stings you, come to me.
OK. Thanks for the warning.

conversations.title: Finding changing rooms, showers, and toilets.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to change and leave her things somewhere.

lines.text: Excuse me, where are the changing rooms?
Behind the beach bar, on the right.
And the restrooms?
Next to the changing rooms.
Are there showers too?
Yes, outside. They're free.
Can I leave my bag somewhere?
There are lockers for 2 euros.

conversations.title: Renting a kayak, paddleboard, or pedal boat.
conversations.scene: Omar and Maya want to go out on the water.

lines.text: Hi. How much is it to rent a kayak?
15 euros an hour for one person, 25 for two.
And a paddleboard?
12 euros an hour.
Do we need any experience?
No, but you must wear a life jacket. It's included.
Where can we go?
Stay inside the bay, please. Don't go past the rocks.
Great. A kayak for two, for one hour.

conversations.title: Asking about the water temperature and sea conditions.
conversations.scene: Yuki doesn't like cold water.

lines.text: How warm is the water today?
About 22 degrees. Not bad!
Is that warm? I'm not sure.
It's cold for one minute, then it's lovely.
Are there big waves?
No, the sea is calm today. Tomorrow there's wind.
Then I'll swim today.
Good idea.

conversations.title: Finding a quieter beach away from the crowds.
conversations.scene: The main beach is too crowded for Maya.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there a quieter beach near here?
Yes, Pine Bay. It's small and very quiet.
How do I get there?
Walk along the coast path for about forty minutes.
Is there a café there?
No, nothing. Take water and food with you.
Is the path easy?
Yes, but wear shoes, not flip-flops.
Perfect. Thanks for the tip!

conversations.title: Ordering drinks or snacks at a beach bar.
conversations.scene: After swimming, Omar is hungry and thirsty.

lines.text: Hi. Two cold lemonades, please.
Large or small?
Large. And do you have anything to eat?
Sandwiches, fries and ice cream.
Two ham sandwiches, please.
Is that to eat here?
No, we're on the sunbeds over there.
OK. I'll bring it to you.

conversations.title: Asking where you can watch the sunset by the water.
conversations.scene: On their last evening in Belmar, Maya and Yuki want to watch the sunset.

lines.text: Where can we watch the sunset by the water?
From the old lighthouse, at the end of the harbor.
What time is the sunset today?
Around 8:30. Go a bit earlier, it gets busy.
Is there anywhere to sit?
There are some benches, and the rocks are flat.
Can we get a drink there?
There's a small bar by the lighthouse.
Perfect. That's our plan for tonight.

conversations.title: Asking which hiking trail is suitable for beginners.
conversations.scene: Maya and Omar want an easy hike near Valdora.

lines.text: Which trail is good for beginners?
The lake trail. It's flat and easy.
How long is it?
Eight kilometers. About two and a half hours.
Is it OK for someone who doesn't hike often?
Yes, it's perfect. There are benches by the lake.
And something a bit harder for tomorrow?
The ridge trail. It's steeper, but the views are amazing.
Let's start with the lake.

conversations.title: Finding out how long a mountain hike takes.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to know if they have time to reach the top.

lines.text: Excuse me, how long does it take to get to the top?
About three hours up, and two hours down.
It's 11 now. Is that too late?
It's OK, but don't stop for too long.
When does it get dark?
Around 8. You have enough time.
Is it very steep?
The last hour is steep. Take your time.
Thanks. Have a good hike!

conversations.title: Asking whether a trail is clearly marked.
conversations.scene: Maya is worried about getting lost.

lines.text: Is the trail to the waterfall clearly marked?
Yes, follow the red and white signs.
Are there signs at every crossing?
Yes, but in the forest they're on the trees.
Do I need a map?
It's a good idea. And download the map on your phone.
Is there phone signal?
Not everywhere. That's why you need the offline map.
Thank you, that's very useful.

conversations.title: Finding the route to a waterfall or scenic viewpoint.
conversations.scene: Omar and Maya come to a crossing with no signs.

lines.text: Excuse me, which way is the waterfall?
Take the path on the left, down into the valley.
How far is it?
About forty minutes. You'll hear it before you see it.
Is there a viewpoint on the way?
Yes, after twenty minutes there's a big rock with a great view.
Is the path difficult?
A little slippery near the water. Be careful.
Thanks a lot!

conversations.title: Asking where you can refill your water bottle.
conversations.scene: Omar's water bottle is empty.

lines.text: Excuse me, where can I refill my water bottle?
There's a fountain in the square, by the church.
Is the water safe to drink?
Yes, it comes from the mountain. It's very good.
Are there other fountains on the trail?
One more, at the hut. After that, nothing.
OK. I'll fill both bottles.
Good idea. It's hot today.

conversations.title: Finding out whether special shoes or equipment are needed.
conversations.scene: Maya isn't sure her sneakers are good enough for the ridge trail.

lines.text: Do I need special shoes for the ridge trail?
Yes, hiking boots. The path is rocky.
Are my sneakers not enough?
For the lake trail, yes. For the ridge, no.
Can I rent boots?
Yes, 10 euros a day.
Do I need anything else?
Walking poles help on the way down. And a jacket. The weather changes fast.
OK, boots and poles, please.

conversations.title: Asking about cable cars or chairlifts to a mountain summit.
conversations.scene: Omar's legs hurt, and he'd like to ride to the summit.

lines.text: Is there a cable car to the summit?
Yes, it leaves every fifteen minutes.
How much is a ticket?
18 euros up, or 28 for a round trip.
How long does it take?
About ten minutes to the top.
When does the last one come down?
At 5:30. Don't miss it!
Two round-trip tickets, please.

conversations.title: Finding a mountain hut where you can eat or rest.
conversations.scene: After a long climb, Maya and Omar reach a mountain hut.

lines.text: Hello. Can we get something to eat here?
Of course. We have soup, sausages and apple cake.
Two soups, please. And can we rest here a bit?
Yes, stay as long as you like.
Is it possible to sleep here?
Yes, we have beds for twenty people. You need to book, though.
How far is it to the summit from here?
One more hour. The path gets steeper.
Then we definitely need the soup first!

conversations.title: Asking whether wildlife is commonly seen in the area.
conversations.scene: Maya sees something move between the rocks.

lines.text: Excuse me, are there many animals in this area?
Yes, deer, foxes and eagles. And marmots up here.
I think I just saw one!
Probably a marmot. They whistle when people come.
Are there any dangerous animals?
Not really. Sometimes snakes in summer, but they're shy.
What should we do if we see a snake?
Just stay calm and walk around it.
Good to know. Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking another hiker for advice about the trail ahead.
conversations.scene: Maya and Omar meet a hiker coming down from the summit.

lines.text: Hi! How is the trail ahead?
Beautiful, but there's still snow near the top.
Is it dangerous?
No, but it's slippery. Walk slowly there.
How long to the top?
About an hour and a half from here.
Is the view worth it?
Absolutely! On a clear day, you can see the sea.
Great. Thanks, and enjoy the way down!

conversations.title: Starting a conversation with another traveler.
conversations.scene: Omar is making coffee in the hostel kitchen when another traveler comes in.

lines.text: Hi! Do you want some coffee? I made too much.
Oh, yes, please! Thank you.
Are you here on vacation?
Yes, for two weeks. I arrived yesterday.
Me too, more or less. How do you like it so far?
I love it. The food is great.
Have you tried the fish soup yet?
Not yet. Is it good?
It's the best. I'm Omar, by the way.

conversations.title: Asking someone where they're from and where they've traveled.
conversations.scene: Omar talks with a traveler on the hostel terrace.

lines.text: Where are you from?
I'm from Canada, but my family is from Morocco. And you?
I'm from Australia.
That's far! Where have you traveled so far?
Thailand, India, and now Europe.
Wow. What was your favorite place?
Hard to say. Maybe the mountains in the north of India.
I'd love to go there one day.

conversations.title: Sharing your travel plans and asking about theirs.
conversations.scene: Omar shares a table on the train with a traveler.

lines.text: Where are you going next?
To the coast, to Belmar. And you?
To the mountains. I want to hike for a week.
Nice! What's your plan after that?
I don't know yet. Maybe the islands.
I'm going to the islands too, next month.
Really? Which ones?
The small ones in the south. My friend says they're quiet.
Send me some tips when you're there.

conversations.title: Asking a stranger to take your picture.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants a photo of herself in front of the bridge.

lines.text: Excuse me, could you take a picture of me?
Sure! With the bridge behind you?
Yes, please. Just press here.
OK. Smile! One, two, three.
Can you take one more, a bit closer?
Of course. How's this?
Perfect! Thank you so much.
You're welcome. Enjoy your day!

conversations.title: Offering to take a group photo for other tourists.
conversations.scene: A group of tourists is trying to take a selfie together.

lines.text: Would you like me to take a photo of all of you?
Oh, yes, please! That would be great.
Everybody closer together. A bit to the left.
Is this OK?
Perfect. Everybody smile!
Can you take one more, just in case?
Of course. Here you go.
Thank you! They're great.

conversations.title: Joining other travelers for a sightseeing activity.
conversations.scene: Two travelers are going on a boat tour, and they invite Omar.

lines.text: We're doing a boat tour this afternoon. Do you want to come?
That sounds fun! What time?
At 2, from the harbor.
How much is it?
20 euros. It's three hours, with a stop for a swim.
Do I need to book?
We booked for four people, and our friend can't come.
Perfect timing! I'm in.
Great. Meet us here at 1:30.

conversations.title: Inviting someone you've just met for coffee.
conversations.scene: After the museum tour, Yuki starts talking to another visitor.

lines.text: That was a great tour, wasn't it?
Yes! I loved the old maps.
Me too. I'm going to get a coffee now.
Can I join you? I'd like a coffee too.
Of course! Let's go to the café downstairs.
Great. I'm Yuki, by the way.
Nice to meet you, Yuki.

conversations.title: Talking about your favorite places and travel experiences.
conversations.scene: Yuki and the other traveler talk about their favorite trips.

lines.text: What's the most beautiful place you've ever seen?
Kyoto in the fall. The trees are red and gold.
That sounds beautiful. I've never been to Japan.
You should go! And what's your favorite place?
Iceland. I saw the northern lights there.
Wow, I'd love to see them.
And what do you like most about this city?
The light in the evening. It's perfect for photos.

conversations.title: Asking someone for their Instagram or contact details.
conversations.scene: At the end of the coffee, Yuki wants to stay in touch.

lines.text: It was really nice to meet you.
You too! Are you on Instagram?
Yes. Can I follow you?
Of course. Here, I'll show you my name.
Got it. I'll send you a message.
Great. And here's my number too.
Thanks! If you visit Japan, tell me.
I will!

conversations.title: Making plans to explore somewhere together the next day.
conversations.scene: Omar and the traveler from the boat tour plan the next day.

lines.text: What are you doing tomorrow?
I want to see the old fortress. Do you want to come?
Sure! What time?
Let's meet here at 9, before it gets hot.
Good idea. Shall we have lunch in the old town after?
Yes. I know a great place behind the market.
Perfect. See you at 9.
See you! Don't be late.

conversations.title: Finding a café with a nice atmosphere.
conversations.place: A street in the old town
conversations.scene: Maya wants a cozy café where she can read her book.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there a nice café near here?
Yes, Café Lina, around the corner.
Is it quiet?
Yes, with old sofas and lots of books.
That sounds perfect. Is it open now?
Until 10 tonight.
Do they have cake?
The best apple cake in town!

conversations.title: Asking where people usually go out in the evening.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to know where people go out at night.

lines.text: Where do people usually go out in the evening?
The old town, around Fountain Square. There are lots of bars.
Is it busy on weeknights?
On Thursdays, yes. On Mondays, it's quiet.
Are there any clubs?
Yes, by the river. They open late.
How late?
Around midnight. Nobody arrives before 1!
Wow, that's late for me.

conversations.title: Finding a bar with live music.
conversations.place: A street in the old town
conversations.scene: Yuki and Maya want to hear live music.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there a bar with live music near here?
Yes, the Jazz Cellar, by the bridge.
What kind of music?
Jazz on Wednesdays, rock on the weekends.
Today is Wednesday! What time does it start?
At 9.
Do we need tickets?
No, but come early to get a table.
Thank you so much!

conversations.title: Asking whether there's an entrance fee or dress code.
conversations.scene: Omar and Nora arrive at a club by the river.

lines.text: Hi. Is there an entrance fee?
Yes, 10 euros, with one drink.
Is there a dress code?
Smart casual. No sports clothes.
Are my sneakers OK?
White sneakers are fine. Not running shoes.
Lucky me. Can we pay by card?
Yes, at the counter inside.

conversations.title: Ordering a drink at a busy bar.
conversations.scene: The bar is full, and Omar wants to order.

lines.text: Excuse me! Two beers, please.
Large or small?
Large, please. And a glass of water.
Anything else?
No, that's all. How much is it?
11 euros.
Can I pay by card?
Yes, here you are.

conversations.title: Finding out what time nightlife usually starts.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to know when the nightlife starts.

lines.text: What time do people usually go out here?
For dinner, around 9. Bars get busy after 11.
That's late! And the clubs?
Clubs start after midnight.
What time do they close?
Around 5 or 6 in the morning.
I'll be asleep by then!
Then go to the bars by the river. They close at 2.

conversations.title: Asking about a local festival happening that evening.
conversations.scene: There are lights and stages everywhere in the city tonight.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there a festival tonight?
Yes, the summer night festival. It's every year.
What happens?
There's music on three stages, and food stands everywhere.
Is it free?
Yes, completely free.
When does it end?
With fireworks over the river, at midnight.
We'll stay for the fireworks!

conversations.title: Finding a place to dance or listen to music.
conversations.scene: Maya and Nora want to go dancing.

lines.text: Where can we go dancing tonight?
Try Studio 9. They play music from the 80s.
Is there somewhere with salsa?
Yes, Club Havana has salsa on Thursdays.
Do they have lessons for beginners?
Yes, at 9, before the party starts.
Perfect. Let's go to the lesson first.
Good idea. I need it!

conversations.title: Asking whether there are any free events tonight.
conversations.scene: Omar is short of money, but he still wants to do something tonight.

lines.text: Are there any free events tonight?
Yes, an open-air movie in the park at 9.
What movie is it?
An old comedy, in the original language with subtitles.
Do I need to bring anything?
A blanket, maybe. And snacks.
Is there anything else for free?
The museum is free on Thursday evenings, until 10.
Today is Thursday! Great.

conversations.title: Finding a safe way back to your accommodation after a night out.
conversations.scene: After a night out, Yuki wants a safe way back to her apartment.

lines.text: Excuse me, how can I get home safely from here?
Where do you live?
Near the university.
Take a taxi. There's a taxi stand on the corner.
Is there a night bus too?
Yes, the N2, but at this time it's every hour.
Then I'll take a taxi. Can you call one for me?
Sure. It'll be here in five minutes.
Thank you so much.

conversations.title: Asking which nearby town or village is worth visiting.
conversations.scene: Maya wants to visit a small town on her day off.

lines.text: Which nearby town is worth visiting?
Rivo, on the lake. It's very pretty.
How far is it?
About an hour by train.
What is there to see?
An old harbor, a castle, and great fish restaurants.
Is it good for one day?
Yes, it's perfect for a day trip.
Thank you, I'll go on Saturday.

conversations.title: Planning a day trip without a car.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to go to the mountains, but he doesn't have a car.

lines.text: Can I visit Valdora without a car?
Yes, there's a direct bus from the main station.
How long does it take?
About an hour and a half.
How often does it go?
Every two hours, from 7 in the morning.
And can I walk around Valdora on foot?
Yes, everything is close to the bus stop.
Great. I'll take the 9 o'clock bus.

conversations.title: Finding out whether a destination can be visited in half a day.
conversations.scene: Nora has a free morning before a meeting.

lines.text: Can I visit the old monastery in half a day?
Yes, easily. It's thirty minutes by bus.
How long do people usually stay there?
About two hours, with the gardens.
So I could be back by 1?
Yes, if you take the 8:30 bus.
Is there a café there?
Yes, the monks sell coffee and cake.
Perfect. I'll go first thing in the morning.

conversations.title: Asking about a scenic train or bus journey.
conversations.scene: Maya wants a beautiful ride, not just a fast one.

lines.text: Is there a scenic train route around here?
Yes, the mountain railway to Valdora. It's famous.
What can you see?
Lakes, bridges and mountains. It goes through twelve tunnels.
Which side should I sit on?
The right side, for the best views.
Is it slower than the bus?
Yes, it takes two hours. But it's worth it.
One ticket for tomorrow morning, please.

conversations.title: Booking a short boat excursion.
conversations.scene: Leon wants to take Timo on a boat trip.

lines.text: Hi. When is the next boat trip to the islands?
At 11. It takes three hours.
How much is it?
30 euros for adults, 15 for children.
Can we see dolphins?
Sometimes! Not every day.
Can we buy food on the boat?
Yes, there's a small bar on board.
One adult and one child, please.

conversations.title: Asking whether a guided excursion includes transportation.
conversations.scene: Omar is thinking about a tour to the waterfalls.

lines.text: Does the excursion to the waterfalls include transportation?
Yes, the bus picks you up at your hotel.
And is lunch included?
Lunch, yes. Drinks are extra.
How long is the whole day?
From 8 in the morning to 6 in the evening.
Is the entrance to the national park included?
Yes, everything except drinks and souvenirs.
OK. Is there a place left for Saturday?
Yes, two places. Shall I book one for you?
Yes, please.

conversations.title: Finding the best place for a picnic outside the city.
conversations.scene: Leon wants to take Timo and Maya for a picnic outside the city.

lines.text: Where's a good place for a picnic outside the city?
The park by the lake, in Rivo. It's lovely.
Is it good for children?
Yes, there's a playground and a small beach.
Can we have a barbecue there?
Yes, in the barbecue area. Bring your own charcoal.
Are there stores nearby?
A small supermarket, five minutes away.
Perfect. Timo will love it.

conversations.title: Asking about local vineyards, farms, or countryside visits.
conversations.scene: Maya and Leon want a day in the countryside.

lines.text: Are there any vineyards we can visit?
Yes, several in the hills, about forty minutes from here.
Do they offer wine tasting?
Yes. A tour and tasting costs about 25 euros.
Can we visit a farm too?
There's a cheese farm nearby. You can see how they make it.
Do we need to book in advance?
Yes, especially on weekends. I can call them for you.
That would be great. Saturday, if possible.

conversations.title: Finding a scenic driving route with interesting stops.
conversations.scene: Leon, Maya and Omar are on a road trip in the rental car.

lines.text: Excuse me, is there a scenic road to Valdora?
Yes, take the old road over the pass. Not the highway.
Is it much longer?
About an hour longer, but much more beautiful.
Are there interesting places to stop?
A castle in the first village, and a viewpoint at the top of the pass.
Is the road in good condition?
Yes, but it has many curves. Drive slowly.
And where can we eat on the way?
The inn at the top of the pass. Their trout is famous.

conversations.title: Asking when the last bus or train returns to the city.
conversations.scene: Maya is enjoying Rivo, but she needs to get back to the city tonight.

lines.text: Excuse me, when is the last bus back to the city?
At 9:40, from this stop.
And the last train?
At 10:15. The station is ten minutes from here.
Do I need to buy the ticket in advance?
For the bus, you buy it from the driver. For the train, at the machine.
Thank you. I'll take the train, then.
Don't miss it. There's nothing after that!

conversations.title: Asking where the most interesting local market is.
conversations.scene: Omar loves markets and wants to find the best one.

lines.text: Where is the most interesting market in the city?
The old market hall. It's 150 years old.
What do they sell there?
Everything: food, flowers, antiques and clothes.
Is it open every day?
Every day except Sunday. Go in the morning.
Why in the morning?
The best things are gone by noon!

conversations.title: Finding shops selling handmade products.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants handmade things, not cheap souvenirs.

lines.text: Are there any shops that sell handmade products?
Yes, on Potters' Street, in the old town.
What kind of things?
Ceramics, jewelry, leather bags and wooden toys.
Are they made there?
Yes, most shops have a workshop in the back.
Can I watch them work?
Often, yes. Just ask politely.

conversations.title: Asking whether an item is genuinely made locally.
conversations.scene: Yuki finds a beautiful bowl, but she isn't sure it's really local.

lines.text: Excuse me, is this bowl made here?
Yes, my husband makes them in our workshop.
How can I be sure? Some shops sell things from factories.
Look at the bottom. There's his signature.
Oh, yes. It's beautiful. How long does one bowl take?
About two days, with painting and firing.
Do you have a certificate?
Yes, every piece comes with a card from the craft association.
Wonderful. I'll take this one.

conversations.title: Buying postcards and asking where to send them.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to send postcards to his family.

lines.text: Hi. Three postcards, please.
Here you are. Anything else?
Do you sell stamps?
Yes. Where are you sending them?
To Canada.
That's 2 euros per stamp.
Where can I mail them?
There's a mailbox outside, on the corner.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking for a recommendation for a small souvenir.
conversations.scene: Maya needs a small gift for her colleagues.

lines.text: Can you recommend a small souvenir?
For a friend, or for your family?
For my colleagues. Something small, for eight people.
These local chocolates are very popular.
Are they easy to carry?
Yes, and they don't melt easily.
How much is a box?
5 euros, or 4 if you buy eight.
Perfect. Eight boxes, please.

conversations.title: Finding a local bookstore with books in your target language.
conversations.scene: Maya is looking for easy books in the local language.

lines.text: Hello. Do you have books for people learning the language?
Yes, the shelf by the window. Easy readers and graded books.
Which level is this one?
That's A2. Short stories, with a dictionary at the back.
Do you have one with audio?
Yes, this one has a code for free audio online.
Great. And a children's book for my neighbor's son?
Try this one. It's very popular with seven-year-olds.
I'll take both, thank you.

conversations.title: Asking to taste a product before buying it.
conversations.scene: Omar sees a stall with many kinds of olives.

lines.text: Can I taste one before I buy?
Of course. Try these green ones.
They're good. A bit salty.
Try the black ones too. They're milder.
Those are perfect. 250 grams, please.
Anything else?
Can I taste the cheese too?
Sure. Here you go.
Delicious. I'll take a small piece.

conversations.title: Finding out whether a market is open on weekends.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to go to the flea market on her last weekend.

lines.text: Is the flea market open on weekends?
Only on Sundays, from 8 to 2.
And on Saturday?
On Saturday, there's the farmers' market in the old town.
What time does it open?
At 7 in the morning.
So early! When is the best time to go?
Before 10. After that, it's very busy.
Thank you!

conversations.title: Asking whether a shop accepts cash or cards.
conversations.scene: Omar wants to buy a leather belt.

lines.text: Do you accept cards?
Sorry, only cash.
Oh. Is there an ATM nearby?
Yes, at the end of the market, by the café.
Can you keep the belt for me?
Of course. I'll put it here for you.
Thanks. I'll be back in five minutes.
No problem.

conversations.title: Asking where to buy regional snacks to take home.
conversations.scene: Before she flies home, Yuki wants snacks to share with her family.

lines.text: Where can I buy regional snacks to take home?
Right here! We have everything from the region.
What do you recommend?
Dried figs, honey cookies and spicy sausage.
I can't take meat on the plane. What about the figs?
The figs travel very well, and they keep for months.
Can you pack them for a flight?
Of course. I'll wrap them well.
Thank you. My family will love them.

conversations.title: Asking a local to recommend something fun to do today.
conversations.scene: Omar knocks on Leon's door on a free Saturday.

lines.text: Leon, what's something fun to do today?
It's sunny. How about the river beach?
I've done that. Something different?
There's a bike tour along the river. You can rent bikes at the bridge.
That sounds great. How long is it?
About two hours, with a stop at a garden café.
Do you want to come?
Yes! Timo and I will come too.

conversations.title: Changing your plans because of bad weather.
conversations.scene: The bike tour is planned, but it's raining heavily.

lines.text: Look at the rain! What do we do now?
Let's change our plans. The bike tour can wait.
Can we go to the swimming pool?
What's open when it rains?
The science museum. Timo loves it.
Yes! The dinosaurs!
OK, and then lunch at the market hall.
Perfect. It's all indoors, so we stay dry.

conversations.title: Asking whether a certain neighborhood is better during the day or at night.
conversations.scene: Maya asks a waiter about the harbor district.

lines.text: Is the harbor district better during the day or at night?
Both, but it's different.
How is it different?
During the day, there's the fish market and boats. It's busy.
And at night?
At night, the bars open and there's music. It's lively.
Is it safe at night?
Yes, the main streets are fine. Avoid the dark parts of the docks.
Thanks. I'll go in the evening, then.

conversations.title: Finding a place to sit and enjoy the view.
conversations.scene: After a long walk, Yuki wants to sit down somewhere nice.

lines.text: Excuse me, where can I sit and enjoy the view?
There are benches on the city wall, just up those steps.
Is the view nice?
Yes, you can see the whole old town and the river.
Is there any shade?
Yes, there are big trees up there.
Perfect. Thank you!
You're welcome. It's my favorite spot.

conversations.title: Asking about a local custom you notice while exploring.
conversations.scene: Maya sees people throwing coins into a fountain.

lines.text: Excuse me, why do people throw coins into the fountain?
It's an old custom. If you throw a coin, you'll come back to the city.
Really? Does it work?
Well, I've lived here all my life!
Do you throw it with your right hand?
With your back to the fountain, over your left shoulder.
Like this?
Perfect. Now you have to come back.
I hope so!

conversations.title: Finding out where to see street performers or local artists.
conversations.scene: Yuki wants to photograph street artists.

lines.text: Where can I see street performers or local artists?
On the old bridge, every afternoon.
What kind of artists?
Musicians, painters, and a man who makes giant bubbles.
Can I take photos of them?
Usually yes, but ask first. And leave a coin if you can.
Is there an artists' market too?
Yes, on the first Sunday of every month, in the park.
Great, I'll go next Sunday.

conversations.title: Asking what people normally do on Sundays in this city.
conversations.scene: It's Sunday, and every store in the city is closed.

lines.text: Greta, why are all the stores closed today?
It's Sunday, dear. Stores are always closed on Sundays here.
What do people normally do on Sundays?
Family lunch, a walk in the park, and coffee and cake.
That sounds nice. Where can I buy bread?
The bakery at the station is open until noon.
Good to know. And what will you do today?
My family is coming for lunch. Would you like to join us?
Really? I'd love to. Thank you, Greta.

conversations.title: Asking someone to explain an interesting object, sign, or building.
conversations.scene: Omar sees a strange metal sign on the wall of a house.

lines.text: Excuse me, can you explain this sign?
It shows how high the water came in the flood of 1890.
So high? That's above my head!
Yes. The whole old town was under water.
And what's the small statue above the door?
A saint. People believed it protected the house.
Are there more signs like this?
Yes, on many houses by the river. Look up when you walk!
I will. Thanks for explaining.

conversations.title: Discovering a beautiful place by accident and asking about it.
conversations.scene: Maya takes a wrong turn and finds a courtyard full of flowers.

lines.text: Excuse me, what is this place? It's beautiful.
It's the old monastery garden. Not many people know it.
Can anyone come in?
Yes, it's open to everyone until sunset.
Who looks after the flowers?
The neighbors. We all help a little.
I found it by accident. I'm so lucky.
The best places are always found by accident.

conversations.title: Asking a local: "If you had only one day here, what would you do?"
conversations.scene: On his last evening, Omar asks Leon the question every traveler asks.

lines.text: Leon, if you had only one day here, what would you do?
Good question! Coffee at the café by the park, first.
Then?
A walk through the old town, and the market.
And lunch?
Fish soup at the harbor, of course.
Of course. And the evening?
The sunset from the castle hill, with friends. Like tonight.
Did someone say sunset? Yuki and I are ready!
Then let's go, all together.

text.title: 300 条真实对话
text.about: 玛雅搬到一座新城市,学习在那里生活:邻居、火车、医生、工作、朋友,然后是海滩、山脉和市场。三十个地方的简短对话,以及你真正需要的短语。
text.maya.about: 玛雅刚刚搬到这座城市去工作。她充满好奇心和礼貌,正在学习这门语言,并且问了很多问题。
text.leon.about: 莱昂住在与玛雅隔昭的大厅对面。他温暖而健谈,喜欢烹饪,而且对城市的每个角落都了解。
text.timo.about: 蒂莫是莱昂的儿子。他七岁,充满疑问,从不静止不动。
text.greta.about: 格蕾塔拥有玛雅的大楼,住在一楼。她善良但严格,她记得一切。
text.nora.about: 诺拉与玛雅合作。她有条理且直接,而且总有计划。
text.yuki.about: 尤基在玛雅的语言课上。她起初很安静,一旦认识她就好笑,而且她从不在没有相机的情况下去任何地方。
text.omar.about: 奥马尔是玛雅的老朋友,他去拜访了几个星期。他很放松,总是充满饥饿,而且他不断失去一切。

text.title: 与人见面
text.introduce-yourself.title: 第一次向某人介绍自己。
text.introduce-yourself.scene: 玛雅在新大楼的楼梯上遇到了一个男人。
text.introduce-yourself.01: 嗨!你在大楼里是新人吗?
text.introduce-yourself.02: 是的,我刚搬进来。我是玛雅。
text.introduce-yourself.03: 很高兴认识你,玛雅。我是莱昂。
text.introduce-yourself.07: 我来自这里。我住在大厅对面。
text.new-neighbor.title: 结识一位新邻居并开始对话。
text.new-neighbor.scene: 玛雅在前门遇到了她大楼的主人格蕾塔。
text.new-neighbor.01: 早上好!你一定是新租客。
text.new-neighbor.03: 我是格蕾塔。我住在一楼。
text.new-neighbor.04: 很高兴认识你,格蕾塔。这是你的花园吗?
text.new-neighbor.05: 是的,我种种西红柿和香草。
text.new-neighbor.07: 谢谢。如果需要什么,就敲门。
text.small-talk-in-line.title: 排队等候时与陌生人闲聊。
text.small-talk-in-line.scene: 玛雅周六上午在面包店排起长队等候。
text.small-talk-in-line.03: 通常。他们的面包是城里最好的。
text.small-talk-in-line.04: 这就是我在这里的原因。你推荐什么?
text.small-talk-in-line.05: 试试黑麦面包。这个时候仍然很暖和。
text.small-talk-in-line.06: 谢谢,我会的。今天天气很美,不是吗?
text.small-talk-in-line.08: 哦,轮到我了。祝你度过美好的一天!
text.introduce-two-people.title: 互相介绍两个人。
text.introduce-two-people.scene: 玛雅正在和尤基一起散步,当他们遇到莱昂时。
text.introduce-two-people.02: 很好,谢谢。莱昂,这是我的朋友尤基。
text.introduce-two-people.03: 你好,莱昂。很高兴认识你。
text.introduce-two-people.07: 没错。你们两人怎么认识彼此?
text.speak-slowly.title: 要求某人重复或说话更慢。
text.speak-slowly.scene: 格蕾塔把垃圾桶告诉了玛雅,但她说话很快。
text.speak-slowly.01: 周二晚上,报纸上的报纸上放了垃圾。
text.speak-slowly.03: 当然。垃圾星期二会掉出来。
text.speak-slowly.04: 星期二。你能重复第二部分吗?
text.speak-slowly.06: 周四的论文。我做对了吗?
text.learning-the-language.title: 说明你正在学习当地语言。
text.learning-the-language.scene: 玛雅在市场上购买苹果,并尝试说这种语言。
text.learning-the-language.03: 你口音很好。你来自哪里?
text.learning-the-language.04: 我来自加拿大。我正在学习这门语言。
text.learning-the-language.06: 谢谢,但我还是个初学者。请慢慢来。
text.compliments.title: 向某人致敬并回应其中。
text.compliments.scene: 上课前,玛雅会看尤基的新照片。
text.compliments.06: 你太善良了。而且我很喜欢你的围巾!
text.compliments.07: 谢谢!那是我妈妈送的礼物。
text.bumping-into-someone.title: 意外撞到某人后道歉。
text.bumping-into-someone.scene: 玛雅正看着她的手机,走进一个拿着咖啡的男人。
text.bumping-into-someone.04: 我没看。很抱歉关于你的咖啡。
text.bumping-into-someone.05: 只是有点压在我袖子上。
text.interrupting-politely.title: 礼貌地打断某人提问。
text.interrupting-politely.scene: 当玛雅需要快速回答时,诺拉正在和同事交谈。
text.interrupting-politely.03: 很抱歉打断了。我可以快速提问吗?
text.interrupting-politely.05: 在哪里可以找到打印机的纸张?
text.saying-goodbye.title: 自然结束对话,告别。
text.saying-goodbye.scene: 玛雅和莱昂在楼梯上聊天,但玛雅必须去。
text.saying-goodbye.01: 那是城里最好的披萨店。
text.saying-goodbye.04: 我会的。好了,我现在该走了。我正在见一个朋友。
text.saying-goodbye.06: 你也是!谢谢你的小贴士。

text.title: 找到你的路
text.directions-to-an-address.title: 向陌生人询问具体地址的路线。
text.directions-to-an-address.scene: 玛雅正在帕克街14号寻找一家牙医诊所。
text.directions-to-an-address.01: 不好意思,我该怎么去帕克街14号?
text.directions-to-an-address.02: 公园街?直接进入交通信号灯。
text.directions-to-an-address.04: 然后向左转。第14位在右边。
text.public-restroom.title: 找到最近的公共厕所。
text.public-restroom.scene: 奥马尔喝了两杯咖啡,需要快点洗手间。
text.public-restroom.01: 不好意思,附近有公共厕所吗?
text.public-restroom.02: 是的,在教堂后面的公园里。
text.public-restroom.04: 价格为50美分。你有硬币吗?
text.public-restroom.06: 然后试试街对面的商场。那里是免费的。
text.how-far-is-it.title: 问一下一个地方有多远,以及到达那里需要多长时间。
text.how-far-is-it.scene: 尤基想步行去山上的城堡。
text.how-far-is-it.01: 不好意思,城堡离这儿有多远?
text.how-far-is-it.04: 大约二十五分钟。很上坡。
text.following-directions.title: 了解涉及街道、转弯和地标的路线。
text.following-directions.scene: 奥马尔询问了去博物馆的路线,并努力记住每一个转弯。
text.following-directions.01: 问吧,城市博物馆是哪条路?
text.following-directions.02: 沿着这条街走,直到看到一座大教堂。
text.following-directions.04: 向右转,然后走左边的第二条街。
text.following-directions.06: 没错。然后穿过桥。博物馆位于公园对面。
text.following-directions.07: 穿过桥,公园对面。明白了!
text.following-directions.08: 你不能错过它。这是一栋黄色的建筑。
text.show-me-on-the-map.title: 请让某人在地图上给你看一个位置。
text.show-me-on-the-map.scene: 玛雅有纸质地图,但她找不到花市。
text.show-me-on-the-map.01: 不好意思,你能在地图上给我看吗?
text.show-me-on-the-map.04: 让我看看。我们在这里,就在车站旁边。
text.show-me-on-the-map.06: 市场就在这里,顺着河边。
text.show-me-on-the-map.07: 你能用我的笔来标记它吗?
text.im-lost.title: 说明你迷路了,需要帮助。
text.im-lost.scene: 奥马尔的手机已经死掉,他根本不知道自己在哪里。
text.im-lost.01: 不好意思,你能帮我吗?我迷路了。
text.im-lost.03: 去我朋友的公寓。在林登街上。
text.im-lost.04: 林登街相当遥远。你知道这个号码吗?
text.im-lost.05: 数字22。我的手机没了,所以无法查看地图。
text.im-lost.06: 乘坐电车3号。第四站下车。
text.im-lost.07: 第三点,第四站。非常感谢!
text.atm-pharmacy-supermarket.title: 查找附近的ATM、药店或超市。
text.atm-pharmacy-supermarket.scene: 玛雅需要现金、一些阿司匹林和牛奶。
text.atm-pharmacy-supermarket.04: 银行旁边有一个绿色十字架。
text.atm-pharmacy-supermarket.05: 太好了。附近还有超市吗?
text.atm-pharmacy-supermarket.06: 是的,但还有一点点。左边有两条街道。
text.safe-at-night.title: 询问一个社区在夜间行走是否安全。
text.safe-at-night.scene: 尤基想从深夜的演唱会上走回来。
text.safe-at-night.01: 晚上穿过老城区安全吗?
text.safe-at-night.02: 是的,通常非常安全。人很多。
text.safe-at-night.04: 没关系,但有些街道相当阴暗。
text.safe-at-night.06: 午夜过后,是的。或者乘坐夜间巴士。
text.street-closed.title: 街道封闭时寻找替代路线。
text.street-closed.scene: 玛雅正在步行去上班,但这条街因市场而关闭。
text.street-closed.01: 不好意思,为什么街道关门了?
text.street-closed.02: 如今有一个街面市场,直到6个。
text.street-closed.03: 我需要去邮局。有别的方法吗?
text.street-closed.04: 是的。走右边的下一条街,四处走走。
text.street-closed.07: 好的。那么对了,然后再又离开了?
text.street-closed.08: 没错。然后你回到了主街上。
text.accessible-entrance.title: 询问最近的电梯、自动扶梯或无障碍入口在哪里。
text.accessible-entrance.scene: 玛雅正在和格蕾塔一起购物,而格蕾塔今天无法走楼梯。
text.accessible-entrance.01: 我的膝盖疼。我今天不能走这些楼梯。
text.accessible-entrance.02: 不好意思,最近的电梯在哪里?
text.accessible-entrance.03: 电梯在后面,旁边是咖啡馆。
text.accessible-entrance.05: 是的,但今天这行不通,抱歉。
text.accessible-entrance.07: 是的,侧门有一个斜坡。我可以为你打开它。
text.accessible-entrance.08: 谢谢,年轻人。那非常善良。

text.title: 在火车站
text.train-ticket.title: 在售票柜台买一张火车票。
text.train-ticket.scene: 玛雅买了一张火车去贝尔马镇的票,那里是沿海地区的小镇。
text.train-ticket.01: 你好。请给贝尔马买张票。
text.train-ticket.03: 请继续往返。我星期天要回来。
text.train-ticket.08: 然后是34欧元。卡片还是现金?
text.train-times.title: 询问火车出发时间和到达时间。
text.train-times.scene: 奥马尔想知道前往贝尔马尔的火车。
text.train-times.01: 下一班火车什么时候开往贝尔马?
text.train-times.06: 是的,每两个小时一次。下一个是12:15。
text.which-platform.title: 为您的火车找到合适的平台。
text.which-platform.scene: 车板显示有两列火车开往贝尔马尔,而玛雅和奥马尔感到困惑。
text.which-platform.01: 看,有两列火车开往贝尔马。
text.which-platform.02: 我们的平台是哪个?让我问一下。
text.which-platform.03: 不好意思,这是10:15到贝尔马的平台吗?
text.which-platform.06: 走下桥,沿着左边的楼梯走去。
text.which-platform.08: 是的,八分钟内就会离开。
text.delay-announcement.title: 了解有关延迟或取消的公告。
text.delay-announcement.scene: 发言者们已宣布,但很难听到。
text.delay-announcement.01: 开往贝尔马的10:15火车延误了大约20分钟。
text.delay-announcement.02: 它说了什么?我们的火车被取消了吗?
text.delay-announcement.03: 不,这是延迟的。大概二十分钟,我想。
text.delay-announcement.06: 现在二十分钟。请收听更新。
text.delay-announcement.07: 对由此带来的不便,我们深表歉意。
text.delay-announcement.08: 那么,是时候喝杯咖啡了。
text.changing-trains.title: 询问是否需要换班。
text.changing-trains.scene: 列车员正在检查玛雅的票,她询问自己的路线情况。
text.changing-trains.02: 你在这里。我需要换火车吗?
text.changing-trains.03: 是的,在卡尔登。换乘区域列车。
text.changing-trains.04: 我在卡尔登有多少时间?
text.changing-trains.05: 十二分钟。火车从同一个站台出发。
text.reserved-seat.title: 找到您的车厢和预留座位。
text.reserved-seat.scene: 奥马尔发现一名女子坐在他的座位上。
text.reserved-seat.01: 不好意思,我觉得这是我的座位。
text.reserved-seat.04: 哦,这是6号车。第二辆车是第二辆。
text.reserved-seat.06: 没问题。这种情况一直发生。
text.validating-tickets.title: 询问有关票务验证和旅行通行证的情况。
text.validating-tickets.scene: 尤基有一张纸质票,但不确定该如何处理。
text.validating-tickets.02: 是的,在上车前请先使用平台上的黄色机器。
text.validating-tickets.03: 如果我忘记会发生什么?
text.validating-tickets.05: 我看。有一周的旅行通行证吗?
text.validating-tickets.06: 是的,每周的通行证费用为25欧元。适用于所有区域列车。
text.luggage-storage.title: 找出存放行李的地点。
text.luggage-storage.scene: 奥马尔有一个大行李箱,在火车开前三个小时。
text.luggage-storage.01: 这里有可以放行李的地方吗?
text.luggage-storage.04: 5欧元用于小型储物柜,8欧元用于大型储物柜。
text.luggage-storage.06: 然后拿一个大的。你在机器上用卡付款。
text.missed-connection.title: 缺少一列连接火车,并请求其他选择。
text.missed-connection.scene: 玛雅的第一班火车已晚,她在卡尔登的联系也不见了。
text.missed-connection.01: 你好。我的火车晚点了,我错过了连接。
text.missed-connection.03: 对贝尔马。火车五分钟前就开了。
text.missed-connection.04: 下一个在一小时内。您的票仍然有效。
text.missed-connection.06: 有一辆公交车在14:20,但你需要一张新票。
text.missed-connection.09: 好的。你能在我的票上写一张纸条吗?
text.missed-connection.10: 当然。有一张邮票,以防万一。
text.lost-on-the-train.title: 报告火车站丢失的物品。
text.lost-on-the-train.scene: 奥马尔把夹克留在了火车上。当然他这么做了。
text.lost-on-the-train.01: 你好。我把夹克留在了火车上。
text.lost-on-the-train.03: 来自城市的10:15。一小时前就到了。
text.lost-on-the-train.05: 深蓝色,口袋里有一个手机充电器。
text.lost-on-the-train.06: 让我来检查一下。不,什么都没有,抱歉。
text.lost-on-the-train.07: 我可以留下我的电话号码吗?
text.lost-on-the-train.08: 是的。填写此表格,我们会联系您。

text.title: 公共汽车和地铁
text.which-line.title: 找到正确的公交线路或地铁线路。
text.which-line.scene: 尤基想乘地铁去上大学。
text.which-line.01: 不好意思,哪条线要上大学?
text.which-line.06: 沿着楼梯走,然后沿着绿色的标牌走。
text.buying-a-bus-ticket.title: 询问在哪里购买公共交通车票。
text.buying-a-bus-ticket.scene: 玛雅在公交站,她没有车票。
text.buying-a-bus-ticket.01: 不好意思,我在哪里可以买一张公交车票?
text.buying-a-bus-ticket.02: 在那边的机器上,或者在应用程序中。
text.buying-a-bus-ticket.04: 不,不再了。仅限机器或应用程序。
text.does-this-bus-stop.title: 询问公交车司机是否在目的地停靠。
text.does-this-bus-stop.scene: 格蕾塔上了一辆她平时不乘坐的公交车。
text.does-this-bus-stop.01: 这辆公交车在医院停吗?
text.does-this-bus-stop.02: 是的,确实如此。这是第六站。
text.does-this-bus-stop.03: 我们到那里的时候能告诉我吗?
text.does-this-bus-stop.04: 确定。您还可以在屏幕上看到止损。
